content: Hypocalcemia is a potential metabolic and nutritional disorder that may occur. Dysgeusia, a nervous system disorder characterized by altered taste perception, may be observed. Paresthesia, another nervous system disorder involving abnormal sensations such as tingling or numbness, may also occur. Patients with a known history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) should not use this product. Individuals with known hypersensitivity to taurolidine, heparin, citrate excipients, or pork-derived products should avoid this product. If HIT is reported, discontinue the product immediately and implement appropriate supportive measures. Drug hypersensitivity reactions may occur; if such a reaction is observed, discontinue the product and provide necessary supportive care. This product is not intended for systemic administration. Maternal use of this product is not expected to result in fetal drug exposure. No animal reproduction studies have been conducted for this product. Breastfeeding while using this product is not expected to expose the infant to the drug. The product is generally considered acceptable for use during pregnancy, as controlled studies in pregnant women have shown no evidence of fetal risk. Taurolidine is a thiazolidinone antimicrobial agent with broad-spectrum activity against gram-positive and gram-negative bacteria, as well as mycobacteria, and it also exhibits antifungal properties. Heparin is an anticoagulant that inhibits activated coagulation factors involved in clotting, particularly factors Xa (at low doses) and IIa (at higher doses). It prevents the formation of a stable fibrin clot by inhibiting the activation of fibrin-stabilizing factor. This product is intended for instillation into central venous catheters (CVCs) only and is not for systemic administration. It should not be used as a catheter lock flush product. To use, withdraw an appropriate volume of the catheter lock solution (CLS) from the vial using a sterile needle and syringe to fill the catheter lumens. Use a 3-mL or 5-mL single-dose vial, depending on the volume of the catheter lumens, to instill the solution into each catheter lumen after every hemodialysis (HD) session. Before the next HD session, aspirate the taurolidine/heparin solution from the catheter and discard it. Each vial is designed for single use with a single patient as a single instillation in a CVC. Discard any unused portion remaining in the vial. Store the product at a controlled room temperature of 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions to 15–30°C (59–86°F). Do not freeze the product.
